question: Which of the following are stored in the form of starch which serves as an internal energy reserve to be used as and when required by the plant?
solution:
The correct answer is **carbohydrates**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Starch** is a complex carbohydrate that plants use to store energy.
 
• It is a polysaccharide that consists of a large number of glucose units.
 
• Plants synthesize starch as a way to store excess glucose, which is a product of photosynthesis.
 
• Starch is found in significant amounts in staple foods like potatoes, wheat, maize (corn), rice, and cassava.
 
• When plants need energy, starch is broken down into glucose molecules, which are then used to produce energy through cellular respiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Starch** plays a crucial role not only in the plant kingdom but also in the human diet as a major source of carbohydrates. It is extensively used in the food industry as a thickener, stabilizer, and filler. Moreover, it serves as a raw material in the production of biofuels and bioplastics, highlighting its importance beyond nutritional aspects.
